Header: Ralstonia solanacearum (syn. Pseudomonas solanacearum ) Bacterial wilt of potato; Chichewa: Chiwawu

Prevention: Do not grow solanaceous plants for 5-7 years in an infected field, because the disease survives that long in the soil.
Practice crop rotation with maize, pigeon pea or cabbage.
Use certified disease-free seed-tubers from registered suppliers as the disease can be spread by infected plant materials.
Obtain seed-potato tubers from areas where the disease does not exist.
Avoid injury to plants as bacteria enter the plant through such sites.
Avoid trespassing, movement of machinery and contaminated tools from infected fields to clean fields.

Keep the field weed-free during crop growth as some weeds host the disease, and ensure fields are kept free of weeds and crops during the dry season as it can help eradicate the bacteria from the soil.
Sterilize the soil by covering the seedbed with black plastic for at least one week before planting.
Prevent runoff/irrigation water from infected fields using a band around the field.
Avoid planting in nematode infested areas as it increases the severity of the disease.
Monitoring: Wilting of plants during day and recovering at night.
Severe wilting of the entire plant despite enough moisture in the soil, stunting and eventual collapse.
Elongated dead spots on the stem.
Brownish slimy ooze when a split tuber is squeezed mechanically (using pair of pliers).
Cut the infected stem and put into a clear glass of water to check for cloudy ooze.
The ooze indicates that it is a bacterial infection.
An infected plant does not have galls on the roots as is the case with nematodes.
The disease spreads fast, hence action must be taken as soon as the disease is noticed.
Direct Control: Rogue out wilted potato plants, dry them and burn or bury them (in a pit of more than 1m deep) outside any fields.
Spot sterilize holes left behind after uprooting infected plants with 1% sodium hypochloride- Bleach (30 kg/ ha) at 20 ml per hole with a jab sprayer.
